newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Construction shares lead in Nigerian bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: Construction shares lead in Nigerian bourse trade.

text.p: Sustained buying helped construction shares to consolidate the previous day's gains in Wednesday trade on the Nigerian stock exchange, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 6819.15 from 6,805.33 on Tuesday.

Leading construction concern Julius Berger rose more than two percent to 7.90 naira from 7.60 naira. G. Cappa was 20 kobo higher at 11.20 naira while Cappa and D'Alberto rose five kobo to touch 6.41 naira.
Breweries continued to do well. Nigerian Breweries climbed 30 kobo to 16.40 naira, and Guinness 20 kobo to 6.70 naira.
In the oil marketing sector Agip rose 25 kobo to 19.75 naira. African Petroleum ended 10 kobo higher at 41.30 while Texaco was 31.31 naira, up 11 kobo.
Cement shares ended mixed. West African Portland Cement Company advanced by 10 kobo to 41.60 naira while Ashaka Cement fell five kobo to 18.30 naira.
A fall in the third quarter profit of Franco-Nigerian conglomerate SCOA did not help the already depressed sector.
The company said on Wednesday that high production costs ate deeply into its net profit for the period to the end of September 1996, although turnover was up appreciably.
SCOA shares were steady at 2.33 naira. But CFAO dropped 10 kobo to 3.30 naira.
Lever Brothers ended the day unchanged just as it did on Tuesday.
Tyre maker Dunlop fell by 30 kobo to 10.00 naira.
